title: Diffusion Alignment as Variational Expectation-Maximization
claim: Alternating between searching for good samples and refitting the model progressively moves the model distribution toward a multi-modal target.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right with block arrows and ellipsis, legend below
description: A horizontal sequence of three 1-D density sketches joined by hollow block arrows, ending in an ellipsis to show repetition. Each panel has a bold title: E-step sampling from the posterior, M-step adjusting the model, then a second E-step from the updated posterior. Black curves show the prior policy p_theta and blue curves show the posterior eta*. In the first panel the black curve has a tall left peak and the blue curve is bimodal. Blue dots mark sampled points, and orange arrows point at them to show test-time search. In the second panel the black curve is reshaped to match the blue one. In the third panel the process repeats with a new posterior. Faint dotted curves show earlier distributions. A bottom legend maps black to prior, blue to posterior and orange to test-time search. The eye goes first to the thick blue and black curves.
caption: Conceptual illustration of DAV. DAV alternates between E-step, where trajectories are obtained via test-time search, and M-step, where the diffusion model parameters θ are updated by amortizing the posterior into the policy. By iterating these two steps, DAV progressively refines the diffusion model toward a multi-modal aligned distribution.
abstract: Diffusion alignment aims to optimize diffusion models for the downstream objective. While existing methods based on reinforcement learning or direct backpropagation achieve considerable success in maximizing rewards, they often suffer from reward over-optimization and mode collapse. We introduce Diffusion Alignment as Variational Expectation-Maximization (DAV), a framework that formulates diffusion alignment as an iterative process alternating between two complementary phases: the E-step and the M-step. In the E-step, we employ test-time search to generate diverse and reward-aligned samples. In the M-step, we refine the diffusion model using samples discovered by the E-step. We demonstrate that DAV can optimize reward while preserving diversity for both continuous and discrete tasks: text-to-image synthesis and DNA sequence design. Our code is available at https://github.com/Jaewoopudding/dav.
